papers.abstract: Small language models are usually built like large ones and then squeezed onto a CPU afterwards. We did the opposite: we fixed the target first, one user, one token at a time, 4-bit weights, ordinary CPU, and chose the architecture to suit it. The result keeps full attention in only 6 of its 18 blocks. The other 12 use short convolutions whose memory is two timesteps wide no matter how long the conversation gets, so two thirds of the network never re-reads a growing cache. Trained from scratch on 59.9B tokens, the model scores 47.31 on a five-task benchmark against a bar of 42.20 that was fixed before training began. It beats GPT-2 124M, Pythia-160M, OPT-125M and GPT-neo-125M, all trained on three to six times more data, and exceeds MobileLLM-125M's published score despite that model seeing a trillion tokens. Validation bits-per-byte is 0.8685. To check the architecture rather than the training recipe, we trained a conventional all-attention model of the same size on the same data, and wrote down the winning condition before scoring either. The hybrid won the chosen quality metric by 0.81%, matched it on downstream tasks, produced a 6.3% smaller 4-bit file, and decoded 1.76x faster at 2048 tokens of context, 2.08x against an external model of similar size. In every measurement the speed advantage is near zero at an empty context and grows with length, which is what the mechanism predicts and what a merely leaner model would not show. A simple bandwidth calculation predicts only 1.17x, so memory volume alone does not explain the gap. We also report what did not work: an unmitigated 4-bit quality cost, roughly half the convolution channels ending up inert and impossible to remove, and a vocabulary larger than this model size warrants.
bullets: Designed for one-user, one-token-at-a-time 4-bit CPU inference rather than compressing a conventional large-model architecture.
Uses 6 attention blocks and 12 short-convolution blocks whose memory remains two timesteps wide regardless of context length.
Scores 47.31 on a five-task benchmark, above the fixed 42.20 target and several similarly sized baselines trained on more data.

Against a same-size, same-data all-attention model, it improves the selected quality metric by 0.81%, matches downstream performance, reduces 4-bit file size by 6.3%, and decodes 1.76× faster at 2048-token context.
Reported limitations include unmitigated 4-bit quality loss, inert convolution channels, and an oversized vocabulary.
papers.selection_reason: Hybrid convolution-attention architecture explicitly designed to avoid re-reading a growing cache and reduce memory footprint for CPU inference, directly targeting efficient attention and KV cache/memory efficiency.
papers.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
papers.tldr: Daedalus-150M is a CPU-oriented hybrid language model that replaces most attention blocks with short convolutions, achieving similar quality with smaller 4-bit storage and substantially faster long-context decoding.

papers.abstract: Attention directly derives normalized information flow from pairwise scores. We introduce Relation, an alternative token-mixing primitive that first organizes pairwise evidence into explicit Self and Exchange relations and derives information flow afterward. This relational organization gives rise to Full Relation, FlashRelation, Linear Relation, Hybrid Relation, and a KV-style Relation Cache. Across matched decoder-only models at approximately 10M, 30M, and 100M parameters, Full Relation achieves lower final validation NLL than MHA at all three scales. In a fixed-context reference benchmark, FlashRelation is 3.60-4.41x faster than the materialized Full Relation implementation. Across scale-matched production workloads, it reaches 76.4-84.9% of PyTorch FlashAttention throughput while executing the Full Relation operator. Hybrid Relation uses 75% Linear Relation layers and achieves strong language-modeling quality. These results support a relation-first view of token mixing: ask Self, ask Others, then let Flow follow Relation.
authors: Yuting Ge, Pengju Yang, Mingkai Nie
bullets: Reframes token mixing as organizing pairwise evidence into Self and Exchange relations, rather than directly deriving flow from attention scores.
Introduces Full, Flash, Linear, and Hybrid Relation variants, plus a KV-style Relation Cache.
Full Relation attains lower final validation NLL than MHA across approximately 10M, 30M, and 100M parameter decoder-only models.
FlashRelation runs 3.60–4.41× faster than materialized Full Relation; Full Relation reaches 76.4–84.9% of PyTorch FlashAttention throughput in production workloads.
Hybrid Relation, using 75% Linear Relation layers, maintains strong language-modeling quality.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces Relation, an efficient alternative to attention for token mixing, with faster implementations and KV-style caching.
papers.title: Ask Self, Ask Others: Relation Is All You Need
papers.tldr: The paper proposes Relation, a token-mixing alternative to attention that explicitly separates self- and cross-token relations before deriving information flow, achieving improved language-modeling loss and efficient implementations across model scales.

papers.abstract: Conventional convolutional kernels are typically defined on fixed discrete grids, limiting their ability to accommodate heterogeneous local structures. Existing adaptive operators improve flexibility but often couple geometric scale variation with content-dependent filtering, while incurring high computational cost from per-location kernel generation. To decouple geometric scale adaptation from content-dependent filtering while avoiding expensive per-location kernel generation, we propose Continuous Relative-scale KAN (Core-KAN), a relative-scale-conditioned continuous convolution operator. Core-KAN maps input features into a compact latent basis space and uses a lightweight scale controller to predict local scales relative to an exponential moving average reference. A KAN-based generator represents depth-wise kernel bases as continuous coordinate functions, allowing the operator to synthesize spatial filters at arbitrary resolutions rather than being confined to a fixed lattice. Instead of synthesizing independent kernels at every location, it constructs a compact bank of scale-conditioned kernel responses and interpolates them according to the predicted local scale map. An independent mixing controller further combines the interpolated basis responses based on local content, explicitly decoupling geometric scale adaptation from content-dependent filtering. Together with lightweight pointwise projections, this design forms a low-rank dynamic convolution that scales efficiently with kernel size and integrates readily into hierarchical vision backbones. Experiments across three representative vision tasks show Core-KAN consistently outperforms strong convolutional and dynamic-kernel baselines with only marginal parameter and computational overhead, offering an efficient, general framework for continuous, scale-adaptive convolution.
authors: Lan Guo, Mengling Li, Haoran Li, Jun Shen, Yuanbo Jiang, Qingguo Zhou, Binbin Yong
bullets: Fixed-grid convolution struggles with heterogeneous local structures, while existing adaptive operators can be costly and entangle scale adaptation with content filtering.
Core-KAN predicts local scales relative to an exponential-moving-average reference and represents depth-wise kernel bases as continuous KAN coordinate functions.
It avoids per-location kernel generation by interpolating a compact bank of scale-conditioned responses at arbitrary resolutions.
A separate content-based mixing controller combines basis responses, forming an efficient low-rank dynamic convolution.
The method integrates into hierarchical vision backbones and reports consistent gains over convolutional and dynamic-kernel baselines with marginal parameter and compute increases.
papers.selection_reason: Continuous scale-adaptive convolution with low-rank dynamic kernels; relevant to efficient vision architectures.
papers.title: Core-KAN: Continuous Vision Kernels with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.tldr: Core-KAN is an efficient continuous convolution operator that separately adapts to local geometric scale and content, outperforming strong baselines across three vision tasks with minimal overhead.

papers.abstract: Standard multi-head attention (MHA) gives every head the same full causal context span, although heads can serve different contextual roles. Some heads may rely mainly on nearby lexical or syntactic context, while others may depend on longer-range relations such as entity interactions, discourse links, or state changes. We present Asymmetric Attention Heads (AAH), a head-wise context- allocation framework that treats context length as an explicit per-head or per-group allocation variable. AAH groups heads using feature-derived statistics, organizes these groups hierarchically, and assigns causal local windows while preserving the standard flat MHA output interface. In 4096- token seed-0 experiments, several AAH-style local-allocation variants achieve lower validation loss than pure full attention. Short-budget ablations show that stable local allocation and head-window assignment structure matter, while fixed/local controls can be competitive with adaptive hierarchy. We interpret AAH as a structured head-wise context-allocation mechanism for quality and analysis, with Attention Coverage Ratio (ACR) reported as a selected-window routing diagnostic
bullets: Motivation: different heads may need different amounts of local or long-range context.
Method: groups heads using feature-derived statistics, organizes groups hierarchically, and assigns causal local windows while preserving standard MHA outputs.
Results: several AAH local-allocation variants outperform pure full attention on validation loss in the reported experiments.
Ablations indicate that stable local allocation and head-window structure matter, though fixed/local controls can match adaptive hierarchy.
Attention Coverage Ratio (ACR) is used to diagnose selected-window routing.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes head-wise context allocation for transformer attention, reducing compute.
papers.title: Asymmetric Attention Heads: Structured Head-Wise Context Allocation for Transformer Attention
papers.tldr: Asymmetric Attention Heads allocates different causal context windows to attention heads, achieving lower validation loss than full attention in seed-0 4096-token experiments.

papers.abstract: Training-free block-sparse attention can accelerate video transformers, but row-wise attention concentration does not by itself specify an executable sparse operator. Queries sharing a block route may have poorly overlapping supports, while retained attention mass alone does not determine the post-softmax error from skipped interactions. We show that partition geometry affects both pooled support and the predictability of the remaining residual from the sparse output. We introduce SparsePR, which combines Response-Coupled Partitioning with Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction. Sampled-query key responses form paired K/V groups, whose centroids induce query-response coordinates for shared routing. A small set of exact query rows then calibrates a call-specific affine correction from the sparse output within the output subspace observed in the probe residuals. Across four heterogeneous video generation and world models, SparsePR consistently reduces attention-reconstruction error. Ablations show that probe fitting accounts for most of this reduction, while response-coupled partitioning lowers hard-drop error and improves reconstruction under a finite probe budget. SparsePR preserves generation quality at 22.0-26.0% realized executed-pair density while achieving 1.48x-2.61x end-to-end speedups. Project page: https://pardistaghavi.github.io/SparsePR-website/
authors: Pardis Taghavi, Reza Langari, Gaurav Pandey
bullets: Problem: Block-sparse routing can group queries with mismatched supports, and retained attention mass does not reliably predict post-softmax reconstruction error.
Method: Response-Coupled Partitioning uses sampled key/value responses to form query-aware routing groups.
Method: Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction fits a call-specific affine correction from a small set of exact query rows.
Results: Across four heterogeneous video models, SparsePR reduces attention-reconstruction error and preserves generation quality at 22.0–26.0% executed-pair density.
Results: It achieves 1.48×–2.61× end-to-end speedups; probe fitting provides most of the error reduction, while partitioning improves hard-drop performance and finite-budget reconstruction.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free block-sparse attention for video generation and world models directly targets efficient attention and video world models.
papers.title: Partition the Support, Reconstruct the Residual: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation and World Models
papers.tldr: SparsePR accelerates video-generation and world-model transformers with training-free sparse attention that reconstructs skipped interactions while preserving generation quality.

papers.abstract: Lightweight proxy models enable rapid experimentation without repeatedly training frontier-scale systems, but their small kernels often leave modern accelerators underutilized. Conventional training compounds this inefficiency by scheduling the forward and backward passes as disjoint phases, so spare capacity in one cannot be filled by work from the other. We reinterpret the detachment mechanism of Forward-Forward (FF) as a scheduling primitive: given a local objective, detaching a block's output removes downstream gradient dependencies, making its backward pass ready when its forward pass finishes. ERASE launches each detached subgraph's backward pass early on a separate CUDA stream, overlapping it with subsequent forward work. Execution trace on a lightweight transformer demonstrates this overlap and its limit: a kernel that saturates the device leaves no capacity for concurrency. On a large-scale click-through-rate model, detaching six dense subarchitectures improves training throughput by up to $9.51\%$ while keeping normalized entropy close to the baseline.
bullets: Lightweight proxy models often underutilize modern accelerators, while conventional phase-separated training leaves spare capacity unused.
ERASE uses Forward-Forward-style detachment to remove downstream gradient dependencies and make each subgraph’s backward pass ready after its forward pass.
Separate CUDA streams overlap early backward work with subsequent forward computation.
Trace analysis shows concurrency is limited when a kernel saturates the device.
On a large-scale click-through-rate model, detaching six dense subarchitectures improves throughput by up to 9.51% while keeping normalized entropy near baseline.
papers.selection_reason: Early backpropagation scheduling overlaps forward and backward passes, a training-efficiency technique transferable to efficient AI.
papers.title: ERASE: EaRly bAckpropagation SchEdule for Faster Training of Modern Recommendation Systems
papers.tldr: ERASE accelerates recommendation-model training by launching detached subgraph backpropagation early to overlap backward and forward computation.
